# Task40 Package A — native friend-lock core

12 October 2026. Standalone native core and public-platform adapters only. The root native mutation modules, reset stores, VPN/service/extension consumers, UI, bridge, backups, subscriptions, app-group policy, sealed candidates and prior evidence are outside this package. No functioning friend lock, adult-mutation enforcement, native phone result or release claim follows from these files.

## Native contract

`enroll(PIN, confirmation, baseline)` requires six ASCII digits twice and an actual native installed-adult baseline/readback supplied later by B/C. It returns success only after protected storage/readback and a native CSPRNG 32-byte recovery key (64 lowercase hex digits) for one-time presentation to the trusted person. PIN and recovery verifiers use distinct 16-byte salts, PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 at 600,000 iterations, 32-byte output, and constant-time equal-length comparison. No plaintext secret is persisted. Swift queues work off the UI thread; Android integrations must use `FriendLockWorker`, whose single process-wide worker never holds an enforcement lock during KDF.

`prepare(nativeExactChange, nativeCurrentConfiguration)` reserves a random 128-bit operation ID and a durable `awaitingSecret` receipt. Keep that operation ID for a response lost during authorization. `authorize(PIN, sameChange, sameConfiguration, operationID)` returns its original authorized/in-flight/completed receipt on exact retries. The convenience form without a prepared ID is for a new request only; it does not establish retry identity after response loss. `claim` durably marks `inFlight`; callers must distinguish completed receipts from permission to execute and revalidate at their actual native mutation boundary. `complete` requires the original request, resulting native configuration revision/generation and actual native readback. A completion retry returns the original receipt only when its result/readback matches. Different deltas/configurations, cancelled IDs, rotation and native invalidation reject replay. Website operations have no app-break type or authority.

An exact change is a known adult-only action plus a bounded native-derived field map: UTF-8, sorted ASCII field names, four-byte big-endian byte lengths, domain `freed-device-adult-change-v1`, action, then sorted key/value pairs. SHA-256 digest is native-generated. Configuration revision and mutation generation are nonempty bounded ASCII tokens. Up to 32 durable operation records are retained; capacity exhaustion rejects additional requests rather than evicting live retry authority. Cancelled IDs remain tombstones until `invalidateAuthorizations` advances the generation and clears them. B/C must invalidate on account transition, repair/newer configuration and cancellation of broader transactions, and keep callback/readback/rollback inside the same native operation. The core cannot observe an OS mutation, decide whether a caller's field map describes the actual delta, or atomically combine a secure-store write with asynchronous OS changes.

Recovery and PIN-authorized credential rotation require a different six-digit PIN, change both verifiers/salts, replace the recovery key, increment lock revision/generation and clear operation records. They do not touch filtering. The successful authenticating credential's throttle clears only in the committed rotation; the other throttle stays intact. Both PIN and recovery attempts reserve a failure count durably before KDF, so interruption or crypto failure consumes an attempt. Delay after failure 5/6/7/8+ is 1/5/15/60 minutes. A successful PIN authorization clears its PIN throttle only with the durable receipt. Native elapsed time advances delay; no wall time is consulted. A new clock session/process/reboot or elapsed rollback retains the entire last persisted remainder, potentially extending delay. This is conservative and must be disclosed in the eventual UI.

## Secure storage and failure semantics

iOS: dedicated `app.freed.device-adult.friend-lock.v1` generic-password Keychain items, non-synchronizable `AfterFirstUnlockThisDeviceOnly`, with a dedicated host-process file transaction lock in excluded-from-backup Application Support. No shared access group or App Group changes. Existing extensions later consume the retained adult-policy baseline rather than secret material.

Android: dedicated AES-256-GCM Android Keystore alias `app.freed.device-adult.friend-lock.aes-gcm.v1`, non-exportable key, randomized 12-byte IV, 128-bit tag and item/domain-bound AAD. Only the first witness write may create the key. Atomic encrypted records live in `noBackupFilesDir/freed-device-adult-security-v1`; explicit file and directory fsync accompany AtomicFile publication. Closing a native lock after verified commit cannot retroactively fail that committed result. An existing key with a missing enrollment witness is a missing-enrolled failure, never fresh state. No account owner, SharedPreferences/private reset, cloud, backup or biometric override is involved. Android's declared minimum API is 24; public PBKDF2WithHmacSHA256 provider availability is documented from API 26. A missing provider returns `cryptoUnavailable`; no lower-cost/custom-crypto/plaintext fallback is used. B/C/D must expose this limitation before enrollment and verify actual supported devices.

Protected `witness`, `record` and `journal` items are distinct. Witness persists once enrollment starts and cannot be removed through this adapter. A fresh all-missing store is `notEnrolled`; missing witnessed record/journal is `missingEnrolled`; unsupported/malformed/bounded-overflow data is `corrupt`; unavailable I/O is `unavailable`. All latter states reject authorization. The retained journal's schema2 envelope has a `prepared`/`committed` phase and at most previous+candidate protected records. Each record is bounded at 65,536 bytes; iOS JSON journal is bounded at 196,608 bytes and Android binary journal at 131,104 bytes. PIN/recovery strings are absent from both generations.

**12 October transaction correction following Root review:** the successful path never deletes the protected journal. Prepared-phase readback precedes candidate record replacement/readback. Publication completes only after committed-phase journal write and native readback. The committed envelope retains both previous and current verifier/throttle/receipt bytes. The next atomic prepared envelope retains the then-current generation and new candidate; older completed generations are bounded away. There is no optional cleanup whose failure can retroactively convert a verified commit into failure. This supersedes the initial delete-journal proposal; no native fixture had been run against that earlier proposal.

A failed pre-commit write/readback returns no success and attempts verified prior-record rollback. A persisted prepared envelope is rolled back before subsequent reads return authority; a failed immediate rollback leaves both records protected for restart recovery. Interrupted first enrollment remains fail closed, with no unauthenticated reset/repair API. A final committed-phase write/readback failure is re-read: a successful write plus observed committed bytes establishes native success, observed prepared bytes recover the prior credential, and unreadable storage or a failed durability write with changed committed bytes yields explicit `commitOutcomeUnknown`. Unreadable storage is status-unavailable. Once storage is readable, native phase/readback resolves the outcome. The old verifier bytes remain recoverable in the retained committed envelope even when the final response is unavailable, but only the authoritative current verifier authenticates normal actions; revoked old secrets do not bypass rotation.

Power loss or callback loss after durable commit can leave the new credential current before its method response arrives. The trusted person knows the submitted new PIN. A lost one-time recovery-key response requires a PIN-authorized rotation to a different PIN/new key. Prepared operation IDs permit exact authorization-response retries without another grant or reusable unlocked flag. While storage cannot be read, no authorization is returned. No OS uninstall/data-removal/tamper-proof guarantee is made.

## Verification reservation and evidence

Failure fixtures were authored before production behavior. Root explicitly deferred native RED/GREEN execution while archive14 attempt2 process group 16407 owned the sole compiler. Root later explicitly released archive14 and reserved the sole compiler for Task40. Final semantic RED guard-removal checks compiled and failed the intended wrong-secret assertion on both platforms. Swift GREEN/macOS frameworks, arm64 iOS15.1 deployment typechecking with existing iPhoneOS26.5 SDK, Kotlin JVM policy/adapter GREEN and Android36 public-framework typecompilation passed. Task40 explicitly released the compiler reservation after all child processes exited. Device secure storage, slow-device KDF timing, signed binary/source binding and native mutation enforcement remain unexecuted. Final check logs and snapshot hashes are retained under this fixture directory. The first strengthened Android filesystem typecheck failed because O_DIRECTORY is absent from the public SDK; the corrected public O_RDONLY + fstat/S_ISDIR + fsync adapter typecheck passed, and the failed attempt remains preserved.

Node-only TypeScript contract typecheck passed on 12 October. Node's independent PBKDF2 known vector for ASCII fixture PIN `123456`, sixteen `0x07` salt bytes, 600,000 rounds and 32-byte output is `0be74e7558e56becceb023ea559588f19bcffe4e9e5ef85d75e02917f383522d`. This is fixture data, not a real enrollment credential. Native fixtures must match that vector before their KDF claims pass.

Run only after Root explicitly reserves one platform:

```sh
node tests/fixtures/friend-lock-core/run-native.mjs --compiler-reserved --platform=swift --red
node tests/fixtures/friend-lock-core/run-native.mjs --compiler-reserved --platform=swift
node tests/fixtures/friend-lock-core/run-native.mjs --compiler-reserved --platform=kotlin --red
node tests/fixtures/friend-lock-core/run-native.mjs --compiler-reserved --platform=kotlin
# Recheck only a changed public Android adapter after unchanged JVM cases have passed:
node tests/fixtures/friend-lock-core/run-native.mjs --compiler-reserved --platform=kotlin --typecheck-only
```

Each invocation is sequential, uses retained fresh temporary copies and never restores/reverts live shared work. RED is a semantic wrong-secret mutation of the temporary core, must compile successfully and fail at the wrong-secret fixture. This proves a negative assertion catches the removed guard; it is not a claim that pre-implementation native RED ran. Fixtures exercise real core/KDF/record-store/Keychain policy/encrypted-envelope code with injected platform I/O; Swift fixtures never instantiate the real system Keychain API, and Kotlin fixtures use JVM AES-GCM rather than the user's Android Keystore. No fixture creates a real Mac/device credential.

Primary API references checked 12 October: [Apple Keychain accessibility](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/security/ksecattraccessibleafterfirstunlockthisdeviceonly), [Android Keystore](https://developer.android.com/privacy-and-security/keystore), [Android SecretKeyFactory](https://developer.android.com/reference/javax/crypto/SecretKeyFactory), [Android AtomicFile](https://developer.android.com/reference/android/util/AtomicFile). Device/runtime proof remains separately required.
